item.title: stats and limbs
item.description:
Most creatures have a race or race/class combo that determines their base stats & limbs. When creating a character, select a race and class from the list of playable races. This race and class combination defines most of your stats for you. See the following guide for all stats to calculate them. What are referenced to as the "3 main stats" are Physical, Mental, and Defensive. These stats are generally combined with the Effort stat in practice, all of which are determined by your race and class. Physical ( determined by race+class ) Mental ( determined by race+class ) Defensive ( determined by race+class ) Effort ( determined by race+class ) * You may select one main stat (Physical, Mental, Defensive) to increase by 1 point during character creation. Vitality (your character's health) has 3 parts to notate: Current Vitality, Maximum Vitality, and Attuned Vitality. Maximum Vitality is calculated by summing the vitality of your limbs. Current Vitality and Attuned Vitality both start equal to your maximum. Max Vitality ( determined by limbs ) Cur Vitality ( = max vitality ) Att Vitality ( = max vitality ) Choose any 3 items from their loot tables to start off with, write these items in your "possessions". These items can include armor. Your armor stat is whatever is listed on your armor. This armor value is the ratio of defensive effort spent to amount of damage reduced. When unarmored or in standard clothing, your armor stat is equal to the 'toughness' determined by your race. Armor ( determined by your equipped armor ) Limbs determine two things: maximum vitality and action slots. Each limb is formatted like the template below, showing the maximum vitality increase and the types of actions it can perform. Something's Appendage. [+3 MV] [Type] - Any custom action(s) this limb can perform.
During your combat turns, you will iterate through your action slots provided by your limbs, spending "effort" to perform an action of that type or one explicitly listed by the limb.

item.title: story skills etc
item.description:
A creature's "story" (as outlined on a creature's sheet) is used to summarize chapters of useful and pivotal experiences into cantos.Each canto signifies a great deal of time, effort, and survival. Select 4 skills to gain or specialize in as a result of these experiences. (select skills that loosely represent your feats and experiences.)A new player-character must select a background for their story to start with. Select one from the list of backgrounds at the end of this section, and write it in your "Story" section like so: Canto 0 : <Type> <Short summary of character background.>Then, be sure to list the skills gained by your background in your "Skills" section. Your character's future experiences will be noted Canto 1, 2, 3 ... Work with the GM to customize your progress in interesting ways. list of backgrounds
These skills are mainly used in downtime actions and roleplay. In New World, downtime actions and skill checks work through these freeform narrative skills instead of stats: Narrative Play: Describe what you do. If the outcome is uncertain or risky, the GM calls for a Skill Check (1d6 + relevant Skill bonus). Downtime Actions: Between active tasks, players get Downtime Actions. Most downtime actions will call for a roll, most of which have an associated skill or skills to assist said action. list of skills Creatures naturally have 5 slots of inventory. A standard Alteri bundle has 10 slots of inventory. Items can take up one or many slots. Some clothing and accessories can add slots, and some larger items may need dedicated equipment to carry.
Next up: downtime

item.title: combat
item.description:
Awareness is what determines the phase-order of the combat. This is a standard combat round's phase-order: Effort Allocation Phase Turn Phase (repeat) When both the enemies and the party are aware of combat starting, begin with the phase-order listed above. In this mutually aware case, turn order starts with whichever party has the creature with the highest Mental stat. When combat begins with an unaware party (either the players or enemies), that unaware party does not partake in the first Effort Allocation Phase. In this exclusively aware case, turn order starts with the "aware" party. In the Effort Allocation Phase creatures in combat clear their action slots, proc "every round" effects, and perform effort allocation. Using this allocated effort, creatures "spend" effort of the main 3 stat types on actions. To allocate effort, we have 3 effort-type buckets. At the start of combat, these buckets start with an amount of effort equal to the creature's related stat value. Then, allocate your pool of allotted effort points into the 3 buckets. * Allocate as many effort points as you have in your effort stat value.
The effort points in these buckets are the resources creatures use to perform different actions. The only way a creature can re-allocate these points is to take the re-allocate action. Turns are taken in clockwise order assuming the players are sitting in clockwise-ascending Mental stat order. However, if the players do not wish to sit in this orientation the GM can choose Left-to-Right, ascending Mental stat order, classic roll-initiative order, etc. The creatures in combat then take their turns clockwise around the table performing actions. Combat turn details are listed below. On your turn, limbs are action slots. Pay an action’s effort cost to perform it, spending a matching limb slot. You may also choose to leave some action slots for the rest of the combat round by simply not using all your actions. In this case, you may perform the "reaction" type actions for those limbs at any time during the round.
Some limbs may be of more than one type, or explicitly list a limb-specific action that it can perform, but generally you will be performing actions from this list of standard actions. Defense action: Spend defensive effort to reduce incoming damage by performing the defensive reaction when being hit in combat. To do this, an arm action slot must be available.
Healing: There are many ways to heal a creature, the limiting resource is your dwindling max vitality between combats. Cur Vitality can be healed up to Max Vitality by rest or items, but cannot exceed it. See "natural rest" downtime action. When talking about plain "Vitality", assume it to refer to Current (Cur) Vitality. Many creatures have exploitable weak points. Declare what you're aiming for -- targeting a specific spot, like a weapon's durability or an existing wound, can pay off with extra damage or a strategic advantage. Status effects have a Count, which determines how many times the effect repeats. Certain Status Effects also have Potency, which determines the magnitude of its effects when applied. Potency and Count are indicated by the status's ratio PotencyCount. * Stack is another word for an applied status effect.
For example, a 32 burn stack has Potency=3 and Count=2, which indicates the enemy will take 3 burn damage for the next 2 turns according to the burn status description.Additionally, when reapplying an existing status, add to both the Potency and Count as if it were a fraction. E.g. 12 + 24 = 36
See list of status effects for more examples. A creature gains a scar when it's reduced to 0 Vitality, or explicitly stated by relevant description. Gaining a scar reduces your Attuned Vitality by 1. See "medical rest" downtime action. Scars can either be attached to a limb, or not explicitly be attached to anything. For the latter, you cannot remove the scar by losing a limb it's attached to. Some scars can be healed by certain downtime actions or items, so be on the lookout for ways to patch up.
Next up: story skills etc

item.title: downtime
item.description: Chunks of non-combat non-roleplay time is spent doing "Downtime Actions" Craft Find Explore Rest etc. Use your skill bonusses on these downtime tasks to determine your effectiveness performing it. E.g. A crafted weapon is guaranteed to do (role) dmg per hit on average w/ it's basic attack. list of downtime actionsCrafting Stuff Roleplay turns are encouraged to go in the same clockwise turn order to encourage everyone their time in the spotlight, as well as allowing the GM to use the pseudo turn-order to manage time-sensitive events during RP.

item.title: define canto
item.description: In literary terms, a canto (from the Italian word for "song") is a major structural division in a long epic or narrative poem—essentially the poetic equivalent of a chapter in a novel.In Dante Alighieri's Divine Comedy, the work is divided into 100 cantos total. Self-Contained: Each canto generally focuses on a specific circle, sub-circle, or encounter. While part of a larger journey, a single canto often features a distinct moral lesson, a specific endeavors, and interactions. Thematic Progression: Moving from one canto to the next signifies deeper descent and escalating narrative stakes, marking clear milestones in the protagonist's transformation.

item.title: list of damage types
item.description: Reduce your vitality by x damage. Reduce your maximum vitality by x damage. ( Your vitality must be less than or equal to this maximum. )Alternate between reducing your vitality and maximum vitality for each point of damage taken (always start with internal). Ex: 3 damage would be 1 external damage and 2 internal damage. Reduce your maximum vitality by x damage. If the damage is greater than the vitality of your lowest vitality limb, apply a burn scar to a random limb.
